subject.title: tools.deny not enforced for claude-cli backend MCP — agents can call denied MCP tools

question: What security semantics should OpenClaw require for per-agent MCP tool policy when a CLI backend consumes generated MCP config directly?
rationale: The expected policy boundary is documented, but the closed direct PR showed a plausible implementation can widen exact MCP allow entries into whole-server access, so automation should not choose the permanent security behavior alone.

options.title: Enforce before handoff without widening access
options.body: Resolve effective per-agent policy before writing the CLI MCP config, include only server-wide or wildcard-safe entries, and fail closed for exact per-tool policies that cannot be represented safely.

options.title: Translate to backend-native deny flags
options.body: Map OpenClaw deny entries into Claude CLI `--disallowedTools` when contract proof shows exact behavior, while keeping generated config filtering for backends without an equivalent deny surface.

options.title: Document and warn only
options.body: Clarify that CLI-native MCP tools are outside OpenClaw enforcement and add doctor/audit warnings, accepting that `tools.deny` remains advisory for this backend path.

recommendation.title: Enforce before handoff without widening access
recommendation.body: Resolve effective per-agent policy before writing the CLI MCP config, include only server-wide or wildcard-safe entries, and fail closed for exact per-tool policies that cannot be represented safely.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on the affected CLI MCP bridge and is the best available owner for the security-boundary decision.
